CanonicalKeywords.rationale: `{ CardKeyword.Retain }` (Restlessness.cs:22) == `retain = True`. A CANONICAL Retain, so no downgrade-rebuild hazard, and load-bearing: the card only works as the last card in hand, so it has to survive the end-of-turn flush to get there.

ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (Restlessness.cs:28-31) == cost 0 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / SELF.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new CardsVar(2)` + `new EnergyVar(2)` (Restlessness.cs:14-18) == both numbers, both declared.

OnPlay.rationale: The condition, the one-at-a-time draws and the order all match. C#'s `IsOnlyCardInHand` is `!Hand.Cards.Except(this).Any()` (Restlessness.cs:26) -- the hand with THIS card removed is empty -- and the sim's `if ctx.player.hand: return` (561-562) is the same test expressed differently, because the sim has already moved the played card out of the hand into the discard-pile limbo (combat.py:452-454), so an empty `hand` means Restlessness was the only card. The draws are issued individually (`for _ in range(self._cards): DrawCmd.draw(ctx.player, 1)`, 563-564) matching C#'s per-card `CardPileCmd.Draw(choiceContext, Owner)` loop (37-40) rather than one bulk draw -- which matters for per-draw listeners such as AutomationPower's counter -- and the energy is gained AFTER the draws on both sides. Presentation, folded in: the energy hover tip (20) and ShouldGlowGoldInternal (24), which reuses the same predicate.
